answer: Open a ticket with SailPoint (Expert Services/support portal) requesting a cloud rule review/deployment for your tenant (give the org name/tenant URL). Attach the rule as a standalone SailPoint Rule XML file (with DOCTYPE sailpoint.dtd, <Rule name="..." type="...">, <Description>, optional <Signature> and the BeanShell inside <Source> wrapped in CDATA). Use one rule per file and name the file after the rule type and rule name, e.g. Rule - AttributeGenerator - Generate Unique Email.xml (convention: 'Rule - <Type> - <Name>.xml'); the name attribute in the XML should match. Prefix rule names consistently with your company/project. Include a short description of the purpose, which source/transform/identity profile it will be attached to, and whether it's new or an update (for an update, reference the existing rule name/ID so it is replaced, not duplicated). Make sure it compiles and was tested locally (e.g., with the rule validator tool) before submitting; SailPoint usually turns reviews around in a few business days. Connector rules (BeforeProvisioning on VA etc.) can instead be uploaded yourself via the /beta/connector-rules API after passing the validator.

No. Cloud rules run in a restricted sandbox: direct use of context (SailPointContext) for getObjectByName, search, saveObject, commitTransaction etc. is rejected in review, as is querying the database directly. Use the provided helper instead: the idn object (IdnRuleUtil). Typical patterns: get the manager via identity.getManager() (if available on the passed-in Identity) and read its attribute with getStringAttribute("email") / getAttribute("email"), or use idn.getIdentityById(managerId) or idn.findIdentitiesBySearchableIdentityAttribute(...) to locate the identity. Better still, avoid the rule entirely: use a transform with the 'getReferenceIdentityAttribute' operation (uid "manager", attributeName "email") in the identity profile mapping. Remember IdentityAttribute rules must be null-safe (manager can be null during first aggregation) and fast, because they run on every identity refresh.

Rejections typically come from: using System.out.println / printStackTrace (writes to stdout, not allowed); creating your own loggers with log4j directly or non-standard logger names; logging at info/debug level inside loops or for every identity (excessive volume on refresh/aggregation); logging sensitive data such as passwords, secrets, tokens, full account/identity attribute maps, PII (SSN, DOB), or the full ProvisioningPlan.toXml() which may contain password AttributeRequests; leaving debug statements that dump whole objects. Accepted practice: use the provided 'log' object (log.debug / log.info / log.warn / log.error), keep messages concise with a rule-name prefix, guard verbose ones with log.isDebugEnabled(), log errors in catch blocks with log.error rather than swallowing, and never log credentials. Connector-rule logs on the VA go to ccg.log, so be especially careful there.

Don't modify the live rule in place. Submit the new version as a separate rule with a new name (e.g., 'Before Provisioning - AD v2') via SailPoint review (or upload with the connector-rules API after validator if it's a connector rule). Once deployed, the new rule exists in the tenant but is not used by anything. When you're ready, switch the source to it by updating the source's beforeProvisioningRule reference (PATCH /v3/sources/{id}, path /beforeProvisioningRule with {type: RULE, id, name}). That swap is instant and reversible: rollback is just re-pointing to the old rule. Test first in a sandbox tenant on the same source config. After stabilization, request deletion of the old rule. Alternatively embed a feature flag in the rule reading a source attribute (e.g., from application.getAttributeValue("useNewLogic")) so you can toggle behavior through source config, but rule versioning plus re-pointing is the cleaner, auditable approach.

Several. 1) countIdentitiesBySearchableIdentityAttribute only supports operations like "Equals" (and StartsWith in some versions); "Contains" is not a valid/efficient operation and gives wrong uniqueness results, plus the attribute must be marked searchable. For uniqueness use "Equals" and also check accounts with idn.accountExistsByDisplayName / idn.attrSearchCountAccounts(sourceIds, "mail", "Equals", values) or isUniqueLDAPValue for AD/LDAP targets. 2) Looping over identity.getLinks() is expensive and frowned upon in review; with many accounts it hurts performance and links may not be loaded. Use idn.getFirstAccountByIdentityId or attribute-specific helpers (idn.getLinkAttribute...) instead. 3) Ensure the uniqueness loop has a max iteration bound (e.g., 100) and throws/returns an error rather than looping forever. 4) Normalize the value (lowercase, strip diacritics/spaces) before checking. Also consider whether a 'usernameGenerator' Create Profile config without a rule suffices.

No. There is no import path for IIQ XML into ISC; the object models differ (no Application, Workflow, TaskDefinition, Rule-runner objects in ISC). Migration is a re-implementation: sources are recreated with ISC connectors (via UI or /v3/sources API, often using SaaS or VA-based connectors), applications/schemas reconfigured, correlation and attribute mappings rebuilt in identity profiles with transforms. Rules must be reviewed: many become transforms or out-of-box configuration; remaining BeanShell is rewritten into supported cloud rule types (submitted to SailPoint) or connector rules (deployed by you via the connector-rules API). IIQ workflows map to ISC Workflows (JSON, built in the visual editor, triggered by event triggers) or external services via event triggers. Use SailPoint's migration tooling/assessment (IIQ to ISC migration assessment) to inventory. Config can then be moved between ISC tenants using SP-Config (sp-config import/export) - but that's ISC-to-ISC only.

AfterProvisioning rules don't exist as a cloud rule type in ISC. Rebuild it as event-driven: subscribe to the 'Provisioning Completed' event trigger (idn:post-provisioning) and implement either an ISC Workflow (trigger: Provisioning Completed, filter for source = AD and operation Disable/accountRequests with op 'Disable', then an HTTP Request action calling the ServiceNow Table API or using the ServiceNow integration) or an external HTTP subscriber (e.g., a small serverless function). Use a JSONPath trigger filter like $.accountRequests[?(@.source.name == 'Active Directory' && @.accountOperation == 'Disable')] to reduce noise. Store ServiceNow credentials securely (workflow HTTP action auth / secrets). Alternatively, use SailPoint's ServiceNow Service Desk integration or Card connector. The AD connector-side AfterModify/AfterDisable native PowerShell rules exist on the IQService, but they're for target-side actions, not ticketing.

Correlation rule: in ISC correlation for authoritative sources is configured in the source's Correlation config (attribute pairs, e.g., identity employeeNumber = account EMPLOYEE_ID); a cloud Correlation rule type exists if logic is too complex, but prefer config. Creation rule (IdentityCreation in IIQ): replaced by the Identity Profile attribute mappings using transforms; complex logic can use an IdentityAttribute rule (cloud rule) referenced from a transform of type 'rule'. Initial lifecycle state, manager etc. are also identity profile mappings (cloudLifecycleState via a transform). ResourceObjectCustomization: becomes a cloud ResourceObjectCustomization? In ISC this exists as a connector rule type 'ResourceObjectCustomization' for VA-based connectors; often replaced by transforms on the identity profile or by BuildMap/JDBCBuildMap (connector rules) for delimited/JDBC sources. Prefer transforms when the change is only for identity attributes.

QuickLinks: ISC has no QuickLinks/custom forms framework like IIQ. Replace with Access Requests (request center), Forms (ISC Forms attached to workflows, Custom Forms), and Workflows with 'Form' actions or launchers (Workflow 'External Trigger' / 'Launchers' let users start workflows from the UI). Custom objects: no Custom object type; store config in source attributes, identity attributes, governance groups, transforms lookups (lookup transform tables), or external storage; workflows can call external APIs. Plugins: no plugin framework in ISC. Re-implement UI functionality as external apps using the ISC APIs (v3/beta) with PATs/OAuth clients, SaaS connectivity custom connectors (SaaS Connector SDK) for integration, event triggers for reactive logic, and the UI Development Kit (UI Dev Kit) for custom portals. Reports: use Search, saved searches/scheduled searches, and Data Access/Access Intelligence or export via APIs.

Business roles with an IdentitySelector rule: ISC roles use membership criteria (Standard criteria on identity attributes, account attributes, entitlements with AND/OR up to limited nesting) or identity list. Translate the rule logic into criteria; if impossible, compute a derived identity attribute (via transform or IdentityAttribute rule) e.g. 'roleEligibility_X' and use it in the role criteria. Role-required access maps to the role's access profiles (entitlements bundled per source). IT roles/bundles don't map 1:1: IIQ IT roles become Access Profiles. CertificationExclusion rules: ISC has no such rule. Use certification campaign filters (campaign filter with inclusion/exclusion criteria on identity attributes, access, sources), campaign scope (search-based campaigns using query exclusions), and identity attribute based filters, plus 'Exclude' options in Manager/Source campaigns. Machine/service accounts can be excluded via filters on identity type or by not correlating them.
